The case of the use of a single X-bar chart applied to the same exact process is treated. Let X be the alignment position of the holes bored in the cylinder blocks. One may suppose that the process has been running long enough so that the variable X is normally distributed with average μ and standard deviation σ; these statistics are used instead of the usual control group. Furthermore, suppose that this process has a Cₚ value of 1 (as is usual for companies in the United States), which means that 3σ = 10 μm. Suppose also that every time the process is stopped, things are corrected in such a way that μ = μ₀ so that the process is under specification as long as it is under control. With these assumptions, one can see that, under Taguchi’s method, the process is stopped every time μ + 10 > μ₀ + 3σ or μ − 10 > μ₀ − 3σ .

In the hypothesized off-line system, instead of measuring a unit every n units, a sample consisting of m = 5 units will be measured every N units – the optimum value of N will have to be found – and the average will be found and denoted X-barᵢ. The variable X-bar will be normally distributed with average μ and standard deviation σ/√(m). The X-bar values will be plotted in a classic X-bar chart, which will serve as a basis for deciding to stop the process or not; this will be done every time X-bar > μ + 3σ/√(m) or X-bar < μ − σ/√(m), which gives an “out-of-control” signal. One can see that this will happen every time the process is stopped under Taguchi’s on-line method so, for this method, the average problem occurrence interval will be v = u = 2570 units.
